key_insight: Training language models on structured experimental evidence enabled stronger perovskite reasoning and guided selection of a contact material used in solar cells reaching 27.05% efficiency.
engineering_relevance: Evidence-grounded AI can help engineers select interface materials and design discriminating experiments for more efficient, thermally stable perovskite solar cells.
method: Reconstruct expert-calibrated evidence records from 4,035 articles, linking strategies, controls and observations to mechanisms.
Adapt OpenPerov using structured evidence; refine selected answers with retrieved evidence in OpenPerov Pro.
Experimentally test an AI-selected K-based self-assembled monolayer analogue against the expert-preferred Na analogue.
evidence_signal: On the 800-question PSM-Bench, OpenPerov Flash ranked first among 13 closed-book systems; experimentally, devices with the selected contact retained 96.74% of initial efficiency after 1,000 hours of dark thermal ageing at 85 °C.
watch_item: Dark thermal ageing does not establish stability under illumination or outdoor operation; broader materials-design validation is still needed.
paper_title: Evidence-grounded large language models guide perovskite solar cell design and optimization
